issues.description: MainPipeline.run() produced map_acceptance.json, map_content_fingerprint.json, preflight validation, and a determinism fingerprint BEFORE junction_link_integrity and map_hygiene run -- both of which can mutate structure (patch links; quarantine/delete roads; modify lanes; repair z-seams/lane-width discontinuities; add G6 lane links) and could even change final_out's path. Pipeline-level acceptance/fingerprints could therefore certify a pre-final XODR.
issues.proof: CONFIRMED with exact line numbers (main_pipeline.py @234e1ef1: acceptance 2315-2326, fingerprint 2336, preflight 2343, determinism 2344 -- all BEFORE junction_link_integrity@2347 and map_hygiene@2389). Mechanically reproduced (not assumed): ordering assertions run against the unfixed file failed with explicit offset evidence; same assertions pass against the fixed file.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: Every downstream consumer of map_acceptance.json/map_content_fingerprint.json (including research campaigns) could have been trusting evidence about a map state that didn't match what's actually on disk as "final". Now fixed: all evidence producers run after both mutating stages, against the actually-published final_out, with a fail-closed ledger detecting stale evidence (wrong path/bytes/invalidated capability).

issues.description: _geom_end() -- LIVE, wired into main_pipeline.py via patch_junction_links/patch_xodr_junction_links -- only recognized <line> and <paramPoly3> planView children. Any road ending in an <arc>, <spiral>, or <poly3> segment fell through to return the segment's START pose (x, y, hdg unchanged), silently treated as a zero-length no-op. Even the paramPoly3 branch always returned the unrotated start heading, never the true endpoint tangent.

Reproduced empirically: arc curvature=0.1, length=10 -- legacy returned (0,0,0), true kernel endpoint is (8.41, 4.60, heading=1.0). TDD integration test added proving a correctly-connected curved-segment road was falsely flagged in suspicious_matches pre-fix.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: Junction-connector distance matching (_road_endpoints -> patch_junction_links) could silently corrupt d_start/d_end for any road ending in a non-line/non-paramPoly3 segment -- risk of picking the wrong predecessor/successor slot, or falsely flagging correct connections as suspicious, in the LIVE production pipeline (not a dormant/dead path like several other findings this session).

issues.description: osm_to_xodr_wrapper.py's Osm2OdrSettings construction never sets proj_string (grep-confirmed: no assignment to settings.proj_string anywhere in the file on current production), so carla.Osm2Odr.convert() silently uses its C++-side default +proj=tmerc +lat_0=0 +lon_0=0 regardless of the OSM data's actual real-world location. center_map also defaults to False (settings dataclass, line 51). An external audit (a separate Gemini-driven full-pipeline verification session, 2026-09-23) reproduced the consequence directly: a produced XODR's header claims EPSG:32632 (UTM 32N, Ingolstadt) but inverse-projecting its header coordinates (840138, 5464923) with the actual-default tmerc params lands at approximately lat 49.24/lon 13.67 -- Czech territory, not Ingolstadt (lat ~48.75/lon ~11.42). The true UTM32N coordinates were separately confirmed as approximately (678800, 5402445) via a corrected-proj_string reference conversion. This is a genuine, current, code-level defect (not stale evidence) -- confirmed by direct grep of origin/integration/production-large-map-20260918's actual file content, not assumed from the external report alone.

The fixing subagent's real (non-mocked) reproduction proved carla.Osm2Odr.convert() genuinely reprojects per proj_string (not metadata-only), and this codebase has an established, already-verified convention -- OSM2ODR_NATIVE_PROJ4 (dem_crs_contract.py) and VERIFIED_XODR_GEOMETRY_CRS_PROJ4 (coordinate_control.py) are both independently confirmed by the coordinator to be the bare tmerc frame (lat_0=0, lon_0=0, k=1, x_0=0, y_0=0, comment: 'verified against WP1 reprojection, 0.0 m'; declared geoReference is provenance-only, not authoritative) -- matching osm_polygon_loader.PROJ_STRING exactly. The real, actually-fixed bug was that proj_string was NEVER assigned at all (behavior depended on CARLA's own undocumented library default, which happened to numerically coincide with the correct frame -- not by design), plus use_offsets was never set False alongside center_map=False (causing a spurious Osm2Odr warning on every conversion). The fix pins proj_string explicitly to the literal osm_polygon_loader.PROJ_STRING string (chosen specifically because stage_04_enrichment.py/main_pipeline.py's georef_proj_consistency check does textual equality against that exact string). A second CARLA-bundled reference script (E:\CARLA\CARLA_0.9.16\PythonAPI\util\osm_to_xodr.py) has the identical missing-proj_string pattern but is not imported/tested by this repo (subprocess last-resort fallback only) -- noted, not modified, out of repo scope. Pre-existing repo files (j5r_coordinate_reconciliation.py, test_coordinate_control_fix.py) already document a ~165,943m 'J5 defect' caused by exactly the misinterpretation the external audit's suggested fix would have reintroduced -- this fix avoids repeating that known failure mode.

issues.description: WriterLock.acquire() performs a genuine TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) race: exists()/is_live() check, then a decision, then an unconditional plain-text write (no O_CREAT|O_EXCL, no atomic rename) -- allowing multiple concurrent agents to all believe they hold exclusive write ownership simultaneously. A second, related bug: a stale (expired-lease) owner's own in-memory WriterLock object can later call .heartbeat() or .release() and unconditionally overwrite a DIFFERENT agent's legitimately-reclaimed lock, because neither method re-validates lock_id/ownership against what is actually currently on disk before writing -- .release()'s owned_by() check only compares against the stale caller's own remembered owner field, never re-reading the live file.
issues.proof: Reproduced with 8 real multiprocessing.Process workers (Windows spawn context, separate interpreters, no GIL masking) released simultaneously via a shared Event, across 25 iterations: 25/25 iterations had more than one simultaneous 'winner' (most had all 8 succeed, ok=8/blocked=0). Second race reproduced via a sequential stale_owner_probe.py: agent-1 acquires with lease_minutes=0 (instant expiry) -> agent-2 correctly reclaims -> agent-1's original stale WriterLock object calls .heartbeat() -> on-disk owner silently reverts from agent-2 to agent-1, and agent-1.release(owner='agent-1') then marks agent-2's still-active lock 'released'.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: This is a shared write-ownership primitive already relied on by merged multi-agent-coordination work (GAP-011 part c's artifact-transaction-integrity system). A real race here means two concurrent agents/processes could both believe they have exclusive write access to the same governed resource at once, or one agent's stale state could silently clobber another's legitimate, still-active lock -- undermining the single-writer discipline this entire production-readiness program depends on.

Suggested direction (not yet approved): switch WriterLock.acquire() to a genuinely atomic create-exclusive primitive (e.g. os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, or an equivalent atomic rename-into-place pattern) -- note that sibling code in the SAME subsystem, Manifest.save() in ultimate_pipeline/artifacts/model.py, already uses the correct pattern (mkstemp + fsync + os.replace), so the concept is already known to this codebase and a consistent fix should mirror it. The stale-owner clobber additionally needs .heartbeat()/.release() to re-read and re-validate the currently-persisted lock_id before writing, not just compare against their own remembered state. This needs explicit sign-off before a fix is dispatched, given the blast radius.

issues.description: detect_undeclared_mutation() only ever examined the CANDIDATE artifact's contents (flagging any element where a forbidden domain string appeared anywhere in candidate.tag/attrib) rather than actually diffing parent vs candidate -- so a forbidden domain that existed UNCHANGED, inherited verbatim from the parent, was falsely flagged as an undeclared mutation even though nothing actually changed there. The function signature itself never received the parent artifact at all; the call site (transaction.py:98) had parent in scope the whole time but never passed it through.
issues.proof: Confirmed via real parent/candidate XODR pairs: case (a) unchanged forbidden domain (byte-identical <junction id="5">, only an unrelated attribute changed elsewhere) -- pre-fix returned True (false positive), confirmed via git stash to re-run the exact pre-fix code. Case (b) genuinely changed forbidden domain (new <junction id="9"> added) -- correctly returned True both before and after the fix.
issues.scientific_runtime_consequence: A candidate artifact carrying forward unchanged, legitimate content from its parent could be wrongly rejected as containing an undeclared mutation, causing spurious promotion failures unrelated to any actual change.

issues_batch_3.description: Formalizes and corrects the earlier 'UE4.26 absent, straightforward install' framing. Attempting the documented CARLA build path (git clone --depth 1 -b carla https://github.com/CarlaUnreal/UnrealEngine.git) fails with 'remote: Repository not found' even though the user's GitHub account is linked to their Epic Games account. This is NOT evidence the repo doesn't exist, and is NOT something Codex (or any automated agent) can resolve -- it is a long-standing, widely-reported, chronic issue across the CARLA community (github.com/carla-simulator/carla issues #6401, #6632, #6681, #7654, #7775, #7826, #9806 -- the most recent dated 2026-07, still unresolved as of this pass). The documented root cause: Epic's GitHub org-invitation flow sometimes silently adds a newly-linked account to a decoy/mirror organization ('EpicGames-Mirror-A') instead of the real Epic Games org that actually has read access to CarlaUnreal/UnrealEngine -- an account can show as 'linked' while still lacking the specific org membership the private repo checks. Multiple affected users report having to explicitly request access to the CarlaUnreal/UnrealEngine 'carla' branch through Epic's own developer forums (forums.unrealengine.com) even after completing the standard account link.
issues_batch_3.proof: Codex: `git ls-remote --heads https://github.com/CarlaUnreal/UnrealEngine.git carla` -> 'Repository not found (128)', 2026-09-23. Cross-referenced against CARLA's own current official documentation (carla.readthedocs.io/en/0.9.16/build_windows/, build_carla/) which still cites this exact clone command as correct/current -- confirming this is an access problem, not a stale/wrong URL.
affected_files: no local artifact affected -- this is entirely an external account/access issue
issues_batch_3.scientific_runtime_consequence: Blocks the entire UE4 cook ladder (GAP-018's own original scope) regardless of code readiness -- no amount of pipeline/package work unblocks this without the engine source itself.
issues_batch_3.owner_subagent: requires the user directly -- verify actual GitHub org membership (Settings -> Organizations; check for the real Epic org vs. 'EpicGames-Mirror-A' or similar mirror/decoy org) and, if in the wrong org, request access to the specific CarlaUnreal/UnrealEngine 'carla' branch via the Unreal Engine developer forums (forums.unrealengine.com) -- this has resolved the issue for other affected users per community reports. Codex correctly declined to proceed with any clone/Setup.bat/build step against an inaccessible repo.
issues_batch_3.residual_risk: HIGH -- entirely gated on the user's own GitHub/Epic org membership being corrected; no code-side or agent-side workaround exists. Do not re-dispatch this to Codex/OpenCode/Gemini again until the user confirms org access is fixed.
